entries.title: The window no longer forces itself above everything
entries.summary: Removed the always-on-top behaviour. The window is parked on the monitor you chose and raised once when it opens, then it behaves like any other window: it goes behind whatever you are doing instead of floating over it. If you play the game fullscreen, alt-tab or windowed mode is how you reach it now.

entries.title: Profiles live in a folder you can find
entries.summary: Profiles now live in a profiles folder beside the executable, and every profile dialog opens there, so picking one no longer depends on where the last file happened to be. A profile.json left over from the old flat layout moves into the folder on the first start, and the move never overwrites a profile you already saved.

entries.title: Keep several profiles and pick them from a list
entries.summary: Save as writes the profile wherever you choose and switches to it, Load opens the Windows file dialog so a profile can live in any folder, and a new Recents list brings back the last five in one click. The status panel always shows which file is in use, and opening one that does not exist now says exactly that instead of failing quietly. Profiles keep the file path they were last saved to, so a portable copy travels with its settings.

entries.title: Space row in the default profile
entries.summary: The shipped profile now ends with a Space row, so the key is ready to bind without adding anything first. Space was already selectable in the key list. Nothing else about the profile changed, so an existing profile keeps its own rows and only gains the new one when you press Reset.

entries.title: Hotkey capture that cannot be hidden, and an explicit Save
entries.summary: Rebinding a hotkey now reads the key at system level and also offers the full key list, so a remapping mouse driver can no longer hide a press. The per-row delete button is gone, so the row list is fixed and Reset restores it. Saving is explicit again: edits live in the session until you press Save, and Load restores the last one. The running version is shown discreetly in the footer.

entries.title: One key to start and stop, and rebindable hotkeys
entries.summary: A single key now starts and stops the presser instead of separate arm and disarm keys, and both it and the quit key can be rebound by pressing Change. The Add row, Fire once and scancode controls were removed.

entries.title: First release: presses your keys on a clock
entries.summary: One row per input with its own interval, sections for tap or hold, a focus gate so it never types into another window, cursor checks so a mouse row cannot click outside the game, and a release guarantee so a held button can never outlive the app. Shipped as a per-user installer with a desktop shortcut and as a portable exe.
